en.name: Garlic powder
en.summary: Garlic powder keeps 3–4 years from purchase in a cool, dark cupboard. It does not spoil — it fades, and it cakes. Moisture is the thing that actually ends a jar, not time.
en.pantry: 3–4 years from purchase in an airtight jar, cool, dark and above all dry. Dried garlic is stable because the water has been taken out of it, and the sulphur compounds that carry its smell survive better than most herb oils, which is why the figure runs to years. The catch is that garlic powder is strongly hygroscopic: it pulls moisture out of a steamy kitchen and sets into a brick. Use a dry spoon, never shake the jar over a pan, and keep it away from the kettle and the hob.
en.fridge: No refrigerated timeline is published for garlic powder, and the fridge is close to the worst place for it. A cold jar opened in a warm room collects condensation every time, and garlic powder cakes faster than almost any other spice on the shelf. A sealed jar in a dry cupboard is what the published figure assumes. If you have a jar that has set solid, that is moisture damage rather than spoilage, and breaking it up usually rescues it.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is published either, and freezing makes the caking problem worse. Garlic powder is one of the longest-lasting things in the spice rack already, so there is nothing to gain. Note also that chopped garlic in oil is a completely different proposition with a genuine safety concern and belongs refrigerated — do not reason from the powder to the jar of wet garlic.
en.thawing: Not applicable — garlic powder is a dry cupboard spice and should not be frozen.
spoilage: A jar set into a solid block, which means moisture has got in.
Little or no smell when you warm a pinch in your palm.
Darkening from pale cream to yellow-brown.
Mould or a musty smell in a jar that got genuinely damp.
tips: Use a dry spoon, every time; a wet one turns the jar to concrete.
Add a few grains of rice to the jar in a humid climate to take up moisture.
Keep it off the shelf above the kettle and away from the hob.
Break up a caked jar with a fork rather than throwing it out.

faq.q: How long does garlic powder keep?
faq.a: 3–4 years from purchase in an airtight jar in a cool, dark, dry cupboard.

faq.q: My garlic powder has gone hard. Is it still usable?
faq.a: Usually yes. Caking is moisture damage rather than spoilage; break it up with a fork and keep the jar drier. A musty smell or mould is a different matter.
No. It is hygroscopic and the fridge is humid, so it will cake. A sealed jar in a dry cupboard is far better.

zh.name: 蒜粉
zh.summary: 蒜粉自購買日起，放在陰涼避光的櫥櫃可放 3～4 年。它不會腐敗——它是淡掉，以及結塊。真正終結一罐蒜粉的是濕氣，不是時間。
zh.pantry: 氣密罐、陰涼、避光，最重要的是乾燥，自購買日起 3～4 年。乾燥大蒜之所以穩定，是因為水分被抽掉了；而帶著蒜味的那些含硫化合物，也比多數香草精油更耐放，這就是為什麼它的數字是以年計。麻煩在於蒜粉極會吸濕：它會把蒸氣瀰漫的廚房裡的水氣拉過來，然後結成一塊磚。請用乾湯匙、不要拿著罐子在鍋子上方抖，並且遠離熱水壺和爐台。
zh.fridge: 蒜粉沒有公布的冷藏期限，而冰箱幾乎是它最糟的去處。冰過的罐子在溫暖房間打開，每一次都會結露，而蒜粉結塊的速度大概是香料架上數一數二快的。公布的數字預設的是密封罐放在乾燥櫥櫃。如果整罐已經結成硬塊，那是受潮而不是腐敗，敲散通常就救回來了。
zh.freezer: 冷凍同樣沒有期限數據，而且只會讓結塊更嚴重。蒜粉本來就是香料架上最耐放的東西之一，沒什麼好賺的。另外要提醒：泡在油裡的蒜末是完全不同的東西，帶有實質的食安疑慮、必須冷藏——不要把蒜粉的邏輯套用到那一罐濕蒜上。
zh.thawing: 不適用——蒜粉是乾燥的櫥櫃香料，不應冷凍。
spoilage: 整罐結成硬塊，代表水氣跑進去了。
在手心搓熱一小撮，幾乎聞不到味道。
真的受潮的罐子長霉或有霉味。
tips: 每次都用乾湯匙；濕湯匙會把整罐變成水泥。
潮濕地區可以在罐裡丟幾粒米幫忙吸濕。
不要放在熱水壺上方的層架，也遠離爐台。
結塊的用叉子敲散就好，不必整罐丟掉。

faq.a: 氣密罐放陰涼、避光、乾燥的櫥櫃，自購買日起 3～4 年。

faq.q: 蒜粉結硬塊了還能用嗎？
faq.a: 通常可以。結塊是受潮而不是腐敗，用叉子敲散、之後保持乾燥即可。有霉味或看得到霉才是另一回事。
不要。它很會吸濕，而冰箱潮濕，冰了就會結塊。密封罐放乾燥櫥櫃好得多。
